schema.title: Livestock Disease Early Detection Symptom & Vitals Schema
schema.disclaimer: SCREENING & TRIAGE AID ONLY — NOT A VETERINARY DIAGNOSIS. Always consult a registered veterinarian for clinical examination, confirmatory testing, and treatment.

symptoms.label: Loss of appetite / off feed
symptoms.description: Animal refuses fodder, concentrate, or grazing

symptoms.label: Severe lethargy or weakness
symptoms.description: Dullness, drooping ears, reluctance or inability to stand

symptoms.label: Sudden drop in milk yield
symptoms.description: Noticeable acute decrease in daily milk production

symptoms.label: Swollen lymph nodes
symptoms.description: Visible/palpable firm lumps in front of shoulder or flank

symptoms.label: Excessive salivation / drooling
symptoms.description: Ropy strings of saliva or foaming from mouth

symptoms.label: Mouth blisters or ulcers
symptoms.description: Fluid-filled vesicles, raw sores, or peeling on tongue/gums

symptoms.label: Nasal discharge
symptoms.description: Watery, thick mucoid, or pus-like discharge from nostrils

symptoms.label: Eye (ocular) discharge
symptoms.description: Excessive tearing, cloudy eyes, or crusty discharge

symptoms.label: Persistent coughing
symptoms.description: Repeated dry or moist cough, especially on movement

symptoms.label: Labored or rapid breathing
symptoms.description: Flared nostrils, stretched neck, open-mouth or heavy abdominal breathing

symptoms.label: Throat or brisket swelling
symptoms.description: Warm, soft fluid swelling under jaw, neck, or chest brisket

symptoms.label: Bleeding from natural openings
symptoms.description: Dark unclotted blood oozing from nose, mouth, or rectum

symptoms.label: Watery or loose diarrhea
symptoms.description: Frequent watery or foul-smelling dung

symptoms.label: Blood-stained diarrhea
symptoms.description: Dark red streaks or frank blood in loose stool

symptoms.label: Left-flank abdominal bloat
symptoms.description: Tight, drum-like distension on the upper left side

symptoms.label: Stopped cud chewing (rumination)
symptoms.description: No visible rumination cycles over several hours

symptoms.label: Sweet / acetone breath odor
symptoms.description: Distinct fruity or nail-polish-like smell on breath or milk

symptoms.label: Firm skin nodules / lumps
symptoms.description: Raised round skin bumps (2-5 cm) on neck, back, or legs

symptoms.label: Hoof sores or foul rot
symptoms.description: Blisters, raw cracks, or foul-smelling decay between claws

symptoms.label: Lameness or limping
symptoms.description: Reluctance to bear weight, stiff gait, or grazing on knees

symptoms.label: Crackling muscle swelling
symptoms.description: Hot painful swelling on thigh or shoulder that crackles when pressed

symptoms.label: Hot, swollen, or painful udder
symptoms.description: Hardened, reddened, or tender udder quarter

symptoms.label: Clotted, watery, or bloody milk
symptoms.description: Visible flakes, clots, pus, or pink discoloration in milk

symptoms.label: Pale inner eyelids
symptoms.description: Whitish or washed-out lower eyelid conjunctiva (anemia sign)

URGENT_REFERRAL.label: Urgent Veterinary Referral Required
URGENT_REFERRAL.summary: High risk of rapid deterioration, fatality, zoonotic hazard, or notifiable herd outbreak. Isolate animal immediately and contact a veterinarian urgently.

VET_CONSULT.label: Prompt Veterinary Consultation (Within 24h)
VET_CONSULT.summary: Requires clinical examination and targeted veterinary therapy. Separate from healthy stock and schedule vet visit within 24 hours.

MONITOR_ROUTINE.label: Supportive Care & Scheduled Vet Review
MONITOR_ROUTINE.summary: Lower immediate mortality risk; provide supportive hygiene/isolation and arrange routine veterinary checkup if signs persist or worsen.

key_indicators: Fever paired with ropy salivation and mouth/tongue blisters
Interdigital hoof lesions causing acute lameness
Rapid spread across multiple animals in the herd
immediate_actions: Isolate affected animals immediately into a separate shaded pen away from healthy stock.
Halt animal movement, shared grazing, and milk/equipment transfer from the shed.
Wash mouth and hoof lesions gently with mild potassium permanganate (0.1%) or alum solution.
Notify the local Government Veterinary Officer immediately (notifiable disease).
do_not: Do not sell, transport, or mix exposed animals with neighboring herds.
Do not force coarse dry fodder; offer soft gruel or clean lukewarm water.

key_indicators: Very high fever (> 40.5°C / 105°F) with sudden onset
Hot, painful swelling of throat, jaw, or brisket
Severe labored breathing and grunting respiratory distress
immediate_actions: Call an emergency veterinarian immediately; death can occur within 12-24 hours without early antibiotics.
Keep the animal quiet in well-ventilated shade to reduce breathing strain.
Segregate from healthy cattle/buffalo and disinfect shared water troughs.
do_not: Do not walk or stress the animal; exertion worsens asphyxiation.
Do not delay veterinary intervention waiting for home remedies.

key_indicators: Firm raised skin nodules (2-5 cm) across neck, back, and udder
Persistent fever with enlarged superficial lymph nodes
Nasal/ocular discharge and sudden drop in milk production
immediate_actions: Isolate affected cattle/buffalo in mosquito- and fly-protected housing.
Apply safe vector repellents (e.g., neem-based sprays) to prevent biting fly transmission.
Report to local veterinary authorities for ring vaccination of healthy herd mates.
do_not: Do not burst or cut skin nodules aggressively; keep open sores clean against maggots.
Do not move infected cattle to livestock markets.

key_indicators: High fever in goats or sheep with thick nasal/eye discharge
Oral ulcers/erosions with foul breath and salivation
Profuse watery or blood-streaked diarrhea leading to dehydration
immediate_actions: Quarantine sick goats/sheep strictly away from the main flock immediately.
Provide oral rehydration solution (clean water + electrolytes) to counter diarrhea fluid loss.
Contact the veterinary dispensary urgently for supportive care and flock vaccination.
do_not: Do not share feeders, water buckets, or bedding with healthy goats/sheep.
Do not introduce new small ruminants into the flock during an outbreak.

key_indicators: Sudden high fever, trembling, or rapid collapse
Dark unclotted blood oozing from nose, mouth, or anus
Sudden unexplained mortality or acute severe distress
immediate_actions: DO NOT TOUCH bare-handed. Restrict people, dogs, and scavengers away from the animal/site.
Immediately alert the District Veterinary Officer and local public health authorities.
Monitor the rest of the herd closely for fever from a safe distance.
do_not: NEVER open or cut open a suspected anthrax carcass — air exposure forms persistent lethal spores.
Do not consume milk or meat from exposed animals.

key_indicators: Hot, painful swelling on heavy thigh or shoulder muscle with crackling feel
Acute severe lameness and high fever in young/adult cattle
Rapid progression of depression and anorexia
immediate_actions: Seek immediate veterinary care for urgent high-dose antibiotic therapy.
Keep the animal immobilized on soft dry bedding.
Schedule clostridial vaccination for unaffected young stock in the herd.
do_not: Do not massage or incise the swollen muscle area without veterinary direction.
Do not leave carcasses unburied in grazing pastures.

key_indicators: Tight, drum-like distension of the upper left flank
Stopped rumination with restlessness or kicking at the belly
Rapidly worsening labored breathing from diaphragm pressure
immediate_actions: Call a veterinarian urgently — acute bloat can cause suffocation quickly.
Remove all lush legume fodder, grain, or water immediately and keep the animal standing/walking gently.
Keep the animal's front end slightly elevated on a gentle slope while awaiting the vet.
do_not: Do not let the animal lie flat on its side.
Do not puncture the flank yourself unless instructed by a veterinarian in life-threatening distress.

key_indicators: Hot, swollen, firm, or painful udder quarter
Clots, flakes, watery secretion, or blood in stripped milk
Sudden milk yield drop with mild-to-moderate systemic fever
immediate_actions: Milk infected cows last and discard abnormal milk safely (not onto shed floor).
Arrange veterinary visit within 24 hours for intramammary/systemic culture-guided therapy.
Apply clean cold/warm compresses as advised and use post-milking teat dip.
do_not: Do not mix milk from the affected quarter into the bulk milk supply.
Do not use unsterile intramammary tubes or random leftover antibiotics.

key_indicators: Fever accompanied by persistent coughing and nasal discharge
Elevated respiratory rate or labored breathing
Dullness and reduced feed intake, often after weather stress or transport
immediate_actions: Move animal to a dry, draft-free, well-ventilated shelter with clean bedding.
Schedule a veterinary checkup within 24 hours for auscultation and targeted therapy.
Ensure easy access to fresh water and monitor rectal temperature twice daily.
do_not: Do not keep the animal in damp, ammonia-heavy, overcrowded sheds.
Do not drench liquids forcibly if coughing/breathing is severe.

key_indicators: Normal or subnormal body temperature in lactating/post-calving stock
Sweet/acetone-like breath odor and sudden drop in milk yield
Weakness, wobbly gait, or reluctance to rise
immediate_actions: Contact a veterinarian within 24 hours for IV dextrose/calcium evaluation.
Provide deep soft bedding and keep the animal upright on its sternum if down.
Offer palatable dry hay and clean water while awaiting veterinary assessment.
do_not: Do not force-drench large volumes orally if the cow is weak or unable to swallow properly.
Do not drag a downer animal across concrete.

key_indicators: Chronic watery diarrhea with normal or mildly low temperature
Pale inner eyelids (anemia) and gradual weight loss
Submandibular fluid swelling ('bottle jaw') over several days
immediate_actions: Collect a fresh fecal sample for veterinary egg-count testing and targeted deworming.
Provide clean drinking water, mineral mixture, and dry stall feeding.
Rotate pasture plots and keep feed off contaminated wet soil.
do_not: Do not repeatedly use the same dewormer without veterinary rotation advice (resistance risk).
Do not ignore pale eyelids in young goats/sheep — severe anemia requires prompt care.

key_indicators: Lameness or grazing on knees without systemic high fever
Foul-smelling decay or moist sores between the hooves
Normal appetite initially unless mobility restricts grazing
immediate_actions: Move affected animals onto clean, dry bedding away from muddy pens.
Clean hooves gently and consult a veterinarian/paravet for proper hoof trimming and zinc sulfate footbath.
Inspect herd mates for early interdigital redness.
do_not: Do not keep animals standing in wet manure/slurry.
Do not confuse with FMD — check the mouth and temperature carefully first.
